sentence: This project studies how cells that migrate along a substrate guide normal skull development and how this process relates to skull defects.
This project tests whether base edits in blood stem cells can treat sickle cell disease and thalassemia without chemotherapy.
This project builds polymers that fight wound infections caused by multidrug-resistant microbes, using computational and machine learning methods.
This project studies blood problems such as bleeding, abnormal blood clot formation, low blood counts and bone marrow failure.
This project studies how the sugar chains on follicle-stimulating hormone change with age and how that affects ovaries and bone in mice.
This project studies what conserved A-rich regions in the untranslated region of Zika virus RNA do and which cellular proteins interact with them.
This project tests whether depression falls into two subtypes, one chronic-intermittent and one time-limited, by following females over time.
This project uses optical techniques to study how signaling molecules change cortical inputs to the basolateral amygdala and control fear and anxiety-related behaviors.
This project maintains and develops a package that studies electrostatic interactions in biological macromolecules and the molecular effects of disease-causing mutations.
This project sets up an instrument that watches individual molecules in real time to see how proteins interact with DNA.
This project builds functional cartilage for laryngotracheal reconstruction using a degradable scaffold that directs cells taken by biopsy to become cartilage.
This project tests gene editing as a treatment for Rett syndrome, a neurodevelopmental disorder caused by mutations in one gene.
This project studies how the immune system is involved in chronic rheumatic diseases.
This project studies amyloid-related imaging abnormalities in squirrel monkeys using neuroimaging, proteomics and neuropathology.
This project studies diseases that affect the oral, dental and craniofacial complex.
This project studies how cancer develops to support the development of cancer treatments.
This project develops gene therapy using Herpes Simplex Virus vectors to carry several genes that reduce brain plaques and clear toxic proteins in Alzheimer’s disease.
This project builds computational tools to study how the sequence, structure and function of long non-coding RNAs relate to each other.
This project studies why animal germline cells fail to divide completely and why nerve cells support stop codon readthrough during translation.
